backlink_pages.author: Priya Sharma

backlink_pages.title: Runbook — Worker Lease Exhaustion
backlink_pages.author: Sam Ortiz
backlink_pages.excerpt: Symptoms Long-running exports hold a lease until the heartbeat expires (NMA-114). Concurrency semaphores leak slots after a panicked handler (NMA-124). Nested null optional fields in job payloads

comments.author: Alex Kim
comments.body: 2M-row export on staging held a single lease for 4m12s with no redelivery. Shipped.

content.text: 2M-row export on staging held a single lease for 4m12s with no redelivery. Shipped.

Long-running export jobs hold a worker lease that is also used for heartbeats. When export CPU work blocks the event loop past the 30-second heartbeat interval, the lease expires and another worker picks up the same job.

Expected: heartbeat continues for the lifetime of the lease holder, independent of export progress, or export work yields often enough to pump heartbeats. Actual: a single synchronous export of a 2M-row workspace blocks for ~90s; the coordinator expires the lease at 30s and redelivers; two workers write partial export files.

Hypothesis: heartbeat ticks run on the same goroutine/event loop as DoExport and never fire while the CPU-heavy encode loop runs. Separate heartbeat thread or lease extension checkpoints inside the encode loop are missing.
Duplicate exports waste storage and occasionally upload truncated CSVs to the customer bucket.
